title: Valid Palindrome
description: A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting all uppercase letters into lowercase letters and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

constraints: s consists only of printable ASCII characters.
hints: Use completely opposite Two Pointers. Check left and right character. Skip if they are non-alphanumeric.

title: Valid Anagram
description: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.
hints: You can sort both strings, but sorting is O(N log N). Try using an integer array map of size 26 to count character frequencies for O(N) time.

title: Longest Common Prefix
description: Write a function to find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings. If there is no common prefix, return an empty string.
hints: Compare the characters of the first string against the corresponding characters of all other strings. Return early as soon as a mismatch occurs.

title: First Unique Character in a String
description: Given a string s, find the first non-repeating character in it and return its index. If it does not exist, return -1.
constraints: s consists of only lowercase English letters.
hints: Pass over the string twice. First, populate a hash map (or size 26 array) with counts. Second pass, find the first index whose count is exactly 1.

title: Isomorphic Strings
description: Two strings s and t are isomorphic if the characters in s can be replaced to get t. All occurrences of a character must be replaced with another character while preserving the order of characters.
hints: Maintain two Hash Maps: one mapping s to t, and another mapping t to s. Both maps must agree.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.
hints: Use the Sliding Window pattern. Expand your 'right' pointer. If you hit a duplicate, immediately shrink your 'left' pointer until the duplicate is evicted from the current window hash map.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description: Given a string s, return the longest palindromic substring in s.
constraints: s consist of only digits and English letters.
hints: Imagine every single index is specifically the 'center' of a palindrome. Start at 'center' and expand outwards left and right for as long as chars match. Don't forget even-length palindromes!

title: String to Integer (atoi)
description: Implement the myAtoi(string s) function, which converts a string to a 32-bit signed integer (similar to C/C++'s atoi function).
hints: Be extremely careful with overflow. If multiplying the integer by 10 throws it past INT_MAX, clamp it! Remember to handle whitespace and exactly one +/-.

title: Group Anagrams
description: Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order.
hints: Two strings are anagrams if their sorted string versions match mathematically. Hash maps keys can be sorted strings, pointing to arrays of strings.
defaultCodeC:
char *** groupAnagrams(char ** strs, int strsSize, int* returnSize, int** returnColumnSizes) {
}

title: Find All Anagrams in a String
description: Given two strings s and p, return an array of all the start indices of p's anagrams in s. You may return the answer in any order.
hints: Uses a Fixed-Size Sliding Window. If the sliding window is the exact length of p, you just compare the alphabet frequency map of the window vs map of p.
defaultCodeC:
int* findAnagrams(char * s, char * p, int* returnSize) {
}

title: Permutation in String
description: Given two strings s1 and s2, return true if s2 contains a permutation of s1, or false otherwise.
constraints: s1 and s2 consist of lowercase English letters.
hints: Essentially identical pattern to Find All Anagrams, but you return `true` immediately as soon as your sliding window matches the character frequency table of s1.

title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Given two strings s and t of lengths m and n respectively, return the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t (including duplicates) is included in the window. If there is no such substring, return the empty string.
hints: Sliding Window pattern! Continuously expand right. Once you have a valid window mapped, lock right and slide left until the window is NO LONGER valid, then go back to expanding right.

title: Regular Expression Matching
description: Implement regular expression matching with support for '.' and '*' where '.' matches any single character and '*' matches zero or more of the preceding element.
hints: Dynamic Programming algorithm (Top Down). If current chars match, proceed. If `*` is hit, DP branch: either use the star to match multiple chars, or ignore star entirely as 'zero occurrences'.

title: Longest Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string containing just the characters '(' and ')', find the length of the longest valid (well-formed) parentheses substring.
hints: Can easily be accomplished holding indices in an integer Stack. Pre-load stack with -1 boundary. On ')', pop the stack and max length is current index minus stack top index.

title: Valid Number
description: Given a string s, return whether s is a valid number. Handles scientific notation, decimals, signage.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, plus, minus, or dot.
hints: Use a Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA) or very strict booleans tracking `seenDigit`, `seenExponent`, and `seenDot`.
